_meta.basis: Fresh 7-project variation runs: Atlas rolling samples 198.23s, 264.63s, 232.93s, 257.64s, 268.74s. Budget keeps cached/watchdog checks strict while allowing variation-heavy React release proof runs; Atlas budget is calibrated to 7-project/4855-file rolling evidence, not single-project watchdog paths.

pipeline.profile_policy: forced cold/release-deep samples are evaluated separately from normal full and cached samples

step_recommendations.recommendation: Keep variation reconciliation out of daily/watchdog profiles and refresh it only for full/release proof or explicit variation work until it gains scoped DNA filtering.
step_recommendations.why: The latest release-deep evidence shows variation analysis as the top wall-clock step; it is valuable merge intelligence, not a live-save requirement.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Keep broad host-merge synthesis out of daily/watchdog profiles and consume existing merge evidence in daily agent packets.
step_recommendations.why: Host merge intelligence reads broad merge/fractal state and was the second-largest cost in the selected budget session.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Prioritize incremental Genome/Atlas scope before adding more parallel workers; verify changed-project filtering in daily and watchdog pulses.
step_recommendations.why: Nuclear remains a truth-layer producer, so skipping it blindly would weaken downstream evidence.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Cache taxonomy/fixture evidence by React capability snapshot and refresh only when Atlas, fixture taxonomy, or support docs change.
step_recommendations.why: The matrix is v1-claim critical, but most inputs are highly cacheable between normal code edits.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Compute health deltas from changed artifacts where possible and reserve full recomputation for full/release profiles.
step_recommendations.why: Health is useful in daily summaries but should not repeatedly rescan broad evidence when the SSOT snapshot is unchanged.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Add/use a release profile that runs deep TSC Oracle only for changed/variant projects or on explicit deep-release runs.
step_recommendations.why: This run spent more time in Oracle than Atlas; it is validation-heavy and not needed for every daily/full analysis profile.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Cache hydrated closure packages by atlas/genome hash and skip unchanged package bodies.
step_recommendations.why: Merge packaging is expensive but strongly hashable after Atlas/Genome generation.

step_recommendations.recommendation: Restrict analysis to projects with Next/App Router signals and cache project-level boundary summaries.
step_recommendations.why: Boundary checks are React-specialist valuable, but broad non-Next scanning costs too much in variation-heavy workspaces.

aggregate_recommendations.recommendation: Cache keyword/gem outputs by Atlas snapshot and project DNA; keep broad rescoring in full/release profiles.
aggregate_recommendations.why: Keyword Stats, Keyword Scanner, and Gem Scorer together represent a large parallelizable but non-surgical cost family.

benchmark_advisories.recommendation: Benchmark CODEMAPS_ATLAS_PROJECT_WORKERS=2 separately before changing defaults; project-level parallelism trades off against per-project AST workers.
benchmark_advisories.why: Atlas already used per-project AST workers and stayed within budget; changing defaults blindly may oversubscribe Node subprocesses.

profile_integrity_recommendation.recommendation: Separate daily/full/release-deep performance profiles so v1 release proof does not pay every enterprise validation cost by default.
profile_integrity_recommendation.why: Profile integrity evidence is missing or failing; without it, heavy release work can leak into live/daily loops.
